column1: # Game profile of Timespinner (Switch, base game 1.0.0 = v0). Plays on the Mac from boot into the first scenes, with sound
# The game's C# runs as C++ compiled by Sickhead's BRUTE (its name is in main), on SDK 7.3.0; its graphics are FNA's OpenGLDevice with MojoShader (main's assertions name
# D:/Projects/Switch/FNA/lib/MojoShader). It renders with NVIDIA's desktop OpenGL through EGL (subsdk0, not loaded): main gets its GL functions from eglGetProcAddress, which the
# host's GL layer implements on Metal (dm/gfx/gl/hle_gl.m). Its sound is XACT (Content/Audio/*.xwb, .xsb, .xgs)
# The shaders are XNA effects (Content/Effects/*.xnb: Direct3D 9 bytecode) that MojoShader turns into desktop GLSL 1.20 at run time: no game file holds the GLSL, so the NSP script
# captures it by booting the game on the Mac (gl_capture.tsv lists it) and dm/gfx/tools/gl_shaders.py translates it offline; the host finds each shader by the hash of its text

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# load order as on Horizon: main, subsdk*, sdk. subsdk0 / subsdk1 are NVIDIA's OpenGL and Vulkan drivers, which program the GPU through NvRm: never loaded, the GL layer answers
# main sets a heap of at most the pool − 64 MB: a 3328 MB heap region. The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory
# no NVN shaders: the NVN tables stay empty (gl_shaders.py writes the GL library and its table, not the profile)

column2: Timespinner has no NVN shaders (its GLSL shaders go through the GL layer)
